newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close down, hurt by tight liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close down, hurt by tight liquidity.

text.p: Thai stocks declined slightly in thin trade on Monday with some investors selling Finance One and large capitalised stocks on tightened liquidity in the money market, brokers said.

"Investors hold not much confidence in the market and there is no fresh news to stimulate investment. Tight liquidity in the money market was the chief reason depressing turnover and I think this situation would remain through this week," said Thanadech Mahapokai of Book Club Finance.
The composite SET index lost 3.04 points to close at 563.35 on 2.5 billion baht turnover.
Traders attributed the tight liquidity to high demand for baht in the offshore market.
Thanadech said liquidity would remain tight in the rest of this week partly due to payment of corporate tax and bank reserve requirement.
Traders said May inflation figures from the commerce ministry were in line with market expectation and they did not create an impact.
The Commerce Ministry said the Thai consumer price index rose 4.3 percent year-on-year in May, unchanged from April.
The SET-50 index shed 0.26 point to 40.89.
Several major sectors retreated on Monday. The finance sector topped the active list losing 2.91 percent, followed by the banking counter shedding 1.14 percent.
Finance One topped the active list, falling 0.70 baht to finish at its daily limit low of 6.30. Bangkok Bank rose one to 152.
